memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Whether it continues flowing from his body or is blocked, it will make him unclean. This is how his discharge will bring about uncleanness:'" - Lev 15:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Whether it continues flowing... or is blocked. Either way, unclean. There was no version of this condition that let the man off.

Read that with sympathy. This was a chronic illness. Not a rash that clears in a week — something ongoing, humiliating, and impossible to hide from those closest to him. And the law made it clear there was no loophole, no better version of his situation to hope for.

Some of you know that ground. The condition that does not resolve. The pain that has outlasted every treatment. The mental struggle that lifts for a season and settles again. You have prayed, and it has not stopped.

Scripture does not pretend that all such things end in this life. Paul asked three times for his thorn to be removed, and God said no — and then said something better: my grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness (2 Cor 12:9).

That is not a cheap answer, and Paul did not receive it cheaply. But it is a true one. God's presence in an unhealed place is worth more than we imagine.

If your discharge has not stopped, God has not stopped either. He is with you inside it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What in your life has not resolved despite prayer?
2. How do you respond when God's answer seems to be "my grace is enough"?
3. Where have you known God's presence inside a difficulty rather than out of it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I bring You the thing that will not go away. Where You do not remove it, make Your grace enough, and let me know Your nearness in the middle of it. Amen.
